main_finding: The screens found useful local mechanisms and important failure modes. They did not establish a breakthrough or a generally reliable memory system.
interpretation: A candidate for the next test combines protected user requirements, an explicit task frontier, selective rule compaction, and source retrieval. This combination remains a proposal. It was not tested end to end.

experiments.name: Five recursive handoffs
experiments.hypothesis: A typed ledger preserves critical facts better than recursive prose under the same size limit.
experiments.finding: Prose passed 9/9 groups. The ledger passed 8/9. It missed a new constraint when first introduced. Both formats exceeded the frozen size maximum.
experiments.classification: Inconclusive: budget control failed. No ledger advantage was observed.

experiments.name: Rule-focused compaction
experiments.hypothesis: A rule-and-exception packet transfers useful relationships to unseen cases within a small packet.
experiments.finding: Both packets answered all 8 unseen release cases correctly. Rule packet: 145 estimated tokens. Summary: 232, above the 220 target. On independent trials, rules used 156 tokens versus 108 for summary. Both retained unknown results.
experiments.classification: Local size benefit on patterned evidence. No prediction advantage. Not a valid equal-size comparison.

experiments.name: Tiny-model weight memory
experiments.hypothesis: A small pretrained model can become useful memory after a short local update.
experiments.finding: Setup reached its time limit before SmolLM2-135M-Instruct weights arrived. No model was loaded. No training or answer generation occurred.
experiments.classification: Inconclusive: setup only. No evidence for or against weight memory.

experiments.name: Query-conditioned retrieval
experiments.hypothesis: Query-shaped source retrieval preserves needed facts better than one compact global packet.
experiments.finding: Retrieval answered all 12 questions with exact sources. The first global packet exceeded its cap. The adaptive capped-packet reader had one substantive answer error after the packet omitted the cooling hold. Batched retrieval exposed a larger union of source records.
experiments.classification: Original comparison is budget-invalid. Adaptive batch result has a context confound.

experiments.name: Task-frontier checkpoint
experiments.hypothesis: A checkpoint preserves resumption state better than a knowledge-focused summary.
experiments.finding: Both arms passed 8/8 fields on one task. On backfill, the checkpoint passed 8/8 and the summary 4/8. All packets met the cap. The checkpoint omitted an unscored instruction not to publish a release.
experiments.classification: Local improvement in scored resumption state. Full requirement preservation failed.

experiments.name: Checked compaction and repair
experiments.hypothesis: A source-backed check and one repair improve aggressive compaction.
experiments.finding: Initial and repaired packets both answered 10/10 hidden groups. The initial packet had 174 estimated tokens. Repair produced 161 against a 160 cap. The repaired packet was rejected.
experiments.classification: Inconclusive: budget failure. No accuracy improvement. Rejection gate enforced the cap.

experiments.name: Isolated retrieval control
experiments.hypothesis: E4 retrieval remains useful when readers cannot see other queries or contexts.
experiments.finding: Separate readers answered 4/4 with retrieval and full history, versus 3/4 with the global packet. The global reader safely returned unknown for an omitted fact. Retrieval used 715 estimated context tokens in total, versus 656 for the global packets.
experiments.classification: Positive local diagnostic. Four selected known queries. No independent confirmation.

experiments.name: No-memory control
experiments.hypothesis: The receiver reproduces all E2 release labels without memory.
experiments.finding: Without memory, release answers scored 0/3 observed and 0/8 unseen. Independent trials scored 0/3 observed and 4/4 unseen because those unseen labels were unknown. Every response was unknown.
experiments.classification: The frozen no-memory hypothesis failed. This does not isolate prior knowledge once a packet is supplied.

limits: The fixtures are constructed. Researchers authored their contracts and graders.
Samples are small. No statistical superiority or general reliability is established.
Only E1 tests repeated handoffs. The other behavior tests mainly use one handoff.
The receivers answer controlled questions. They do not execute full native agent tasks.
E4's exact-format scores reject some semantically correct answers. The unchanged scores and manual review remain available.
E4's capped arm, E7, and E8 are adaptive diagnostics on known fixtures.
A passing grader can miss important source requirements, as E5 demonstrated.
All packet sizes use o200k_base estimates. Native usage includes substantial CLI overhead.
Orchestration, setup, training, storage, and worker inference are separate resource categories.
No experiment establishes extraction of unique fundamental truths or equations.
next_experiments: Test a protected requirement store plus task frontier over ten actual interrupted tasks. Check every user constraint.
Compare adaptive choice of prose, rules, and retrieval on new task families. Keep each receiver isolated.
With pretrained weights available before the timer starts, compare raw-history and verified-answer updates under an equal training-token budget.
Add late exceptions to an apparent shared rule. Measure correction, uncertainty, and retention across further handoffs.

worker_accounting.note: These counts exclude parent and subagent orchestration. The successful setup probe is separate. Packet sizes use o200k_base estimates. They are not total model-call costs.
